test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 25th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. B and C together can complete it in 30 days. If the efficiency of A is twice that of C, then in how many days will B alone complete the same work?
solution:
Given:

A and B together can do a piece of work in 24 days. B and C together can complete it in 30 days

The efficiency of A is twice that of C.

Concept used:

Total work = Work done per day × Total time taken

Calculation:

LCM (24, 30) = 120 units

Let efficiencies of A, B, and C be represented by A, B, and C respectively.

So, A = 2C

According to the question,

A + B = 120/24

⇒ A + B = 5

⇒ 2C + B = 5 ....(1)

B + C = 120/30

⇒ B + C = 4 ....(2)

(1) - (2),

2C + B - B - C = 5 - 4

⇒ C = 1

Putting C = 1 in (2),

B = 3

Now, B will alone complete the work in = 120/3

⇒ 40 days

∴ B alone will complete the work in 40 days.
